title: Physiological and Perceived Relief Provided by Passive Back-Support Exoskeletons During Simulated Nursing Tasks
summary: This study investigates how two selected models of passive back-support exoskeletons can reduce physical strain during typical nursing tasks. To this end, healthy adults perform three standardized movement tasks that simulate key lifting and support activities common in everyday care work—once without an exoskeleton and once with each of the two exoskeleton models. Measurements include energy expenditure, heart rate, perceived exertion, and wearing comfort.
conditions: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are among the most common work-related health problems in the nursing profession. Repetitive tasks such as repositioning, supporting, and transferring patients under ergonomically unfavorable conditions frequently lead to chronic overload of the musculoskeletal system, particularly in the lumbar spine. Consequences include pain-related movement limitations, absenteeism, and, in many cases, premature exit from the profession. As a result, the preventive reduction of physical strain in nursing has become a growing focus of occupational health and workplace intervention strategies.  Passive back-support exoskeletons offer an innovative approach to reducing lumbar load during physically demanding nursing tasks. Their physiological and ergonomic effects are currently being investigated in both laboratory and real-world settings. In this study, healthy, physically active individuals with professional experience in nursing are examined under standardized conditions to objectively assess the acute effects of two different passive exoskeletons. The inclusion of healthy participants allows for an isolated analysis of cardiovascular, muscular, and perceptual responses to exoskeleton use, without confounding factors such as pre-existing conditions, pain symptoms, or mobility impairments. The results aim to inform occupational health perspectives on the short-term effectiveness and preventive potential of passive exoskeletons in nursing-related work environments.

interventions.name:
Condition 1: Without Exoskeleton
Participants complete three standardized 5-minute lifting tasks (repositioning in bed, assisting from lying to sitting, and transferring from bed to chair) without wearing an exoskeleton. A standardized warm-up phase is conducted prior to the tasks. Individually tai

Condition 2: Auxivo Lift Suit
Participants wear the "Lift Suit" exoskeleton (Auxivo) during the movement tasks. The procedure is otherwise identical to Condition 1.

Condition 3: Hunic Care Exo Lift
Participants wear the "Care Exo Lift" exoskeleton (Hunic) during the movement tasks. The procedure is otherwise identical to Condition 1.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- healthy individuals
- at least 6 months of professional experience in nursing
Exclusion criteria:
any cardiovascular disease; any pulmonary disease; acute viral or bacterial infections and communicable diseases; lack of willingness or ability to cooperate (non-compliance); physical, mental, or other conditions preventing the provision of required information or participation in study procedures; pregnancy; current participation in another clinical study
